result:
Post revisions are implemented. `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (18 tests, 16 of them new), and `bunx guren gate` is green on all six stages. Nothing is committed; the changes are in the working tree.

One behaviour you should know about: a save that changes nothing still keeps a revision. The task left this open, and I chose the single rule "every successful save adds one revision" over comparing content, so an author who saves twice gets a duplicate entry in the history.

## Summary

I added a `post_revisions` table (`db/schema.ts` plus the generated migration `db/migrations/20260929175238_create_post_revisions/`) and a `PostRevision` model. `app/Models/Post.ts` gained two methods: `Post.revise()` copies the stored title, excerpt and body into a revision and then updates the post in one transaction, and `Post.purge()` deletes a post's revisions along with the post. `PostController.update` and `destroy` now call these, so creating a post and refused edits keep nothing. The new `app/Http/Controllers/PostRevisionController.ts` serves `GET /posts/:id/revisions` (newest first, rendering the new `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx` page through `PostRevisionResource`) and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore`. Both routes are registered in the auth group in `routes/web.ts`, so guests are redirected to `/login`, and both authorize with the existing `PostPolicy.update`, so non-authors get 403. A restore looks the revision up by id and post id together, so a revision of another post answers 404. The post page (`resources/js/pages/posts/Show.tsx`) links to the history for the author, `PostValidator.ts` has the new params schema, the `.guren/*.gen.ts` manifests are regenerated, the tests are in `tests/PostRevisionController.test.ts`, and the decisions are recorded in `docs/adr/0002-keep-post-revisions-on-every-edit.md`.
